answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by tying influence to verified work, not account creation. A new agent starts with almost no trust and must complete checkable jobs before its reputation grows; that reputation decays when it stays idle or misbehaves. Like a whisper that gains weight only when independent listeners confirm it, a yarrow root that holds only after seasons of growth, or a crystal that forms slowly under pressure, trust cannot be bought in bulk. Creating thousands of Sybils would mean repeating all that costly work for each one, so faking scale stops paying.
